monuments in County Wicklow through the Community Monuments Fund 2026.

Funding of nearly €170,000 allocated for Wicklow’s Historic Buildings 
Wicklow County Council welcomes the recent announcement from the Department of Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage of capital funding for two properties in County Wicklow under the Historic 
Structures Fund (HSF). 
Russborough House, Blessington has been awarded €101,817, while the Old Schoolhouse, Lacken has 
secured €66,433 for conservation repairs to the historic fabric. 
Russborough House is a building of National importance and a key visitor attraction for County Wicklow, 
operated by the Alfred Beit Trust. The HSF grant will support a programme of extensive and essential 
stone repairs to secure the continued role of the structure as a heritage, educational and community 
asset. 
The Old Schoolhouse in Lacken has been at the heart of community life in the village for more than 150 
years, initially as a national school, and more recently as a community centre. The HSF funded 
conservation works will include repair of timber windows, overhaul of cast-iron rainwater goods, lime 
repointing, stone repairs and re-rendering in lime plaster. 
The HSF scheme is co-ordinated by Wicklow County Council on behalf of the Department of Housing, 
Local Government and Heritage. The core aims of this fund are to enable larger scale conservation works 
to be carried out on historic structures which are deemed to be significant and in need of urgent support, 
encourage the regeneration and reuse of historic structures, and to support the conservation of historic 
structures for community benefit. 
HSF funded works promote the use of traditional materials and craft skills, supporting employment in 
specialist conservation trades and aligning fully with the aims of the scheme to enable larger-scale 
conservation, sustain heritage skills, and build climate resilience in historic structures.

Energy Retrofit Program 
As part of our ongoing Energy Efficiency retrofit programme, housing services are undertaking works across 
the county. This includes, depending on house surveyed, and not limited to external wall insulation, attic 
insulation, heat pumps and upgraded windows and doors. These works comply with our policy on energy 
fabric upgrades which went through the SPC in 2023. 
The driver of this programme is the improvement to energy efficiency of local authority properties (BER – 
B2 or better), energy cost savings and sustainability. The move from solid fuel to more sustainable, energy 
efficient and cost-effective heating systems contributes to the climate change agenda and dramatically 
improves the comfort levels of tenants in these properties. 
A new Framework has been developed and contracts are moving towards tender stage to deliver on 
projects in 2026, in line with DHLGH requirements.

The Homeless HAP Place finder provides assistance in: 
• 
seeking out potential properties suitable for households currently identified as homeless or at risk 
of homelessness. 
• 
liaising with specific households to establish their specific needs. 
• 
establishing relationships with local property agents and landlords; and, 
• 
supporting those homeless households to (a) prevent the necessity to enter emergency 
accommodation or (b) to exit emergency accommodation and secure a tenancy. 
• 
To date, 702 households (490 families & 210 singles) have been assisted under the Homeless 
HAP Scheme in Wicklow County Council from the inception on 1 st October 2018 to 30 th April 
2026. (270 homeless cases, 384 prevention cases to date and 48 direct provision).   177 
properties were sourced by WCC. 
 
Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in danger 
of becoming homeless.  
There are 10 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous 
transition by the clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to making 
them all ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months. 
Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam 
Road, Wicklow as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed units, 
and two 3-bed units.  
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary 
Accommodation) with key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into 
Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term accommodation.   
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of 
emergency/cold weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). There is 
on site key working support linking in with clients.

Housing First 
Peter McVerry Trust has been appointed as the Housing First Programme Implementer for the Mid-East 
Region. Wicklow County Council is committed to working with them and has now reached and surpassed 
the targets identified in the programme. Housing First recognises that a stable home provides the basis for 
recovery in other areas.  
 
Properties will be provided by both Wicklow County Council and Peter McVerry Trust for the implementation 
of the programme. 
Wicklow County Council has, to date, successfully accommodated 19 clients under Housing First.  Other 
clients proposed for Housing First have been assessed by the team and are availing of key support work 
pending finalisation of sourcing of accommodation. The main issue facing this programme is the availability 
of 1-bed units in suitable locations with easy access to required services.

Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.
